title: Symlink resolution in osf check and scan
summary: Adds a shared `symlink` module that decides what a symlink means to the scanner: a link whose real target lives inside the repository is followed to the real files behind it, while a link pointing outside the repository, into `.git`, at nothing, or in a loop is refused with a named error. `osf check` now expands links before its existence check, and the directory walk in `osf scan` follows in-repo links instead of counting them as skipped, so a linked skills folder or a symlinked scan path is actually read.

lanes.subtitle: osf binary

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: check <name> [paths...]
nodes.summary: Parses the check name and the explicit paths, then hands them to the check dispatcher. Unchanged by this diff, but it is where a refused symlink surfaces as exit code 2.

nodes.label: run_check
nodes.subtitle: fn run_check(name, opts, files, gate)
nodes.summary: Now expands symlinks before the existence check for Scan, LintWriting and LintSkill, so a linked path is validated against the real files behind it rather than the link itself. ScanStaged and ScanCommits are untouched.

nodes.label: ensure_files_exist
nodes.subtitle: not-found contract
nodes.summary: Still the single place that turns a missing path into a user-facing error. It now sees the expanded list, so a missing plain path still errors while a link that resolved to real files does not.

nodes.label: expand_links
nodes.subtitle: fn expand_links(root, files) -> Vec<String>
nodes.summary: Entry point used by check: canonicalizes the repository root, passes plain and missing paths through unchanged, replaces each symlink with the repository-relative paths of the real files behind it, and de-duplicates first-seen wins.

nodes.label: resolve_link / resolve_link_from
nodes.subtitle: fn resolve_link(root, link)
nodes.summary: Resolves a link to one (label, real) pair per file behind it. A file target yields one pair; a directory target is walked. Refuses a target outside the repository or inside .git, a dangling link, and a loop over an ancestor directory.

nodes.label: follow
nodes.subtitle: fn follow(link, label)
nodes.summary: Walks the symlink chain itself, resolving relative targets against the link's parent and tracking seen link identities so two links pointing at each other are caught as a loop rather than spun on.

nodes.label: inside_repository
nodes.subtitle: root prefix, minus .git
nodes.summary: The containment predicate: the real target must start with the canonical root and must not start with the root's .git folder. This is the boundary that makes an outside link a refusal instead of a read.

nodes.label: walk_dir
nodes.subtitle: sorted, .git skipped, nested links resolved
nodes.summary: Walks the real directory behind a link, sorting entries for stable output, skipping .git, and applying the same resolve rules to any nested link so a link inside a linked folder is not a hole in the policy.

nodes.label: collect_files
nodes.subtitle: fn collect_files(root, path, out)
nodes.summary: Previously counted a symlink into `skipped` and never read it. Now calls resolve_link and pushes the (label, real) pairs, so an in-repo link found while walking a scanned folder contributes its real files.

nodes.label: resolve_scan_targets
nodes.subtitle: fn resolve_scan_targets(dir, paths)
nodes.summary: Drops the skipped counter from its return and threads the repository root into collect_files. Git-tracked mode is unchanged: tracked symlinks are still excluded later rather than followed.

nodes.label: scan_files
nodes.subtitle: reads targets, applies excluder
nodes.summary: Reads each (label, real) target, skips binaries, applies the excluder, and reports findings. Its contract is unchanged; what changed is the list of targets it receives.

nodes.label: symlink unit tests
nodes.subtitle: inside, outside, loop, dangling, .git, dedup
nodes.summary: Ten unit tests covering the resolution rules directly: inside directory and file expansion, outside refusal, parent loop, mutual links, dangling link, plain and missing pass-through, .git refusal, and first-seen de-duplication.

nodes.label: check integration tests
nodes.subtitle: follow, refuse, linked skills dir
nodes.summary: End-to-end tests through the CLI: a linked directory with a leak is scanned and reported, an outside link and a loop exit 2 with `symlink refused`, and the .claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills layout lints clean instead of reporting file not found.

nodes.label: scan integration tests
nodes.subtitle: followed, refused, cycle
nodes.summary: The three symlink tests are inverted: an explicit symlinked directory is now followed and its finding reported, while a nested link pointing outside and a cycle are now refusals rather than silent skips.

edges.label: expand before existence check
edges.summary: The change that makes a linked path a first-class input: expansion happens before the not-found check, so the check validates the real files rather than the link.

edges.label: containment gate
edges.summary: The single predicate that separates follow from refuse: inside the canonical root and outside .git.

edges.label: nested link
edges.summary: Recursion back into the same rules, so a link inside a linked folder is held to the same containment and loop checks.

edges.label: link found while walking
edges.summary: Replaces the old `skipped += 1`: a link encountered during a directory walk now contributes its real files instead of being counted and dropped.

edges.label: (label, real) targets
edges.summary: The target list now carries real paths behind links; the skipped counter is gone from the return type.

flows.title: An explicit symlinked path is expanded before the check runs
flows.summary: What happens when a user or CI names a symlink on the command line: the link is resolved against the repository root, refused if it escapes, and the real files behind it are what the check actually reads.

messages.label: containment + loop checks
messages.note: Refuses with `symlink refused: <link> points outside the repository`, `points at nothing`, or `loops`; otherwise returns one (label, real) pair per file behind the link.

response.shape: repository-relative forward-slash paths, de-duplicated first-seen wins

messages.label: expanded path list
messages.note: A missing plain path still passes through and still errors here; a link that resolved to real files does not.

views.title: Symlink resolution across check and scan
views.summary: The new resolution module sits between the check dispatcher and the scanner, and is called from two places: the explicit-path expansion in check, and the directory walk in scan.

views.title: Inside the resolution module
views.summary: The containment predicate and the chain follower are the two decisions the whole policy rests on; walk_dir recurses back through them for nested links.

children.title: Tests pinning the policy
children.summary: Unit tests exercise the rules directly; integration tests drive them through the CLI and through scan_paths.

views.title: Explicit symlinked path, end to end
views.summary: The ordered path from a named link on the command line to the real files being scanned, including the refusal branch.
